name: Assault (bodily injury to a public servant)
conduct: Intentionally, knowingly or recklessly causing bodily injury to another. Bodily injury includes physical pain, illness or impairment of physical condition. The actor knows the person is a public servant and the person is lawfully discharging an official duty, or the assault is in retaliation for or on account of official power or duty. Public servant has the broad definition in §1.07(a)(41), including specified government officers/employees, jurors and other listed roles. This ordinary public-servant choice excludes the more specific peace-officer/judge second-degree circumstance; a person’s status alone does not replace the required duty connection. The distinctive-uniform/badge knowledge presumption requires its facts and does not compel guilt. The consent defense in §22.06 requires effective consent or a reasonable belief in consent and its injury/risk conditions; it is unavailable for the specified criminal-street-gang initiation or continued-membership conduct. Other justification and case-specific defenses require separate review.
penalty: Third-degree felony: ordinarily two to ten years in prison and a possible fine up to $10,000. Qualifying prior convictions or other statutory findings can change punishment. The separate aggravated-assault offense and its additional elements are not decided by this choice.

name: Assault (bodily injury to a sheriff, constable, municipal officer or DPS officer)
conduct: Intentionally, knowingly or recklessly causing bodily injury to another. Bodily injury includes physical pain, illness or impairment of physical condition. The actor knows the person is a peace officer, and the officer is lawfully discharging an official duty, or the assault is in retaliation for or on account of official power or duty. Peace-officer status is limited here to sheriff/deputy, constable/deputy, municipal-police/marshal and DPS roles meeting article 2A.001(1)-(4), unchanged in both published versions. Other peace-officer categories remain unresolved by this choice. This is second-degree bodily-injury assault, not the separate deadly-weapon/serious-injury aggravated-assault offense. The consent defense in §22.06 requires effective consent or a reasonable belief in consent and its injury/risk conditions; it is unavailable for the specified criminal-street-gang initiation or continued-membership conduct. Other justification and case-specific defenses require separate review.
penalty: Second-degree felony: ordinarily two to 20 years in prison and a possible fine up to $10,000. Qualifying prior convictions or other statutory findings can change punishment. The separate aggravated-assault offense and its additional elements are not decided by this choice.

name: Assault (bodily injury by a civilly committed actor against commitment-office personnel)
conduct: Intentionally, knowingly or recklessly causing bodily injury to another. Bodily injury includes physical pain, illness or impairment of physical condition. The actor must be committed to a civil commitment facility, defined as a state/vendor facility housing only persons civilly committed as sexually violent predators under Chapter 841 and know the victim is an officer or employee of the Texas Civil Commitment Office, while lawfully discharging an official duty or in retaliation for or on account of official power/duty. This special provision applies to all three assault forms, overriding ordinary threat/contact misdemeanor grades. Subsection (d-1) supplies a distinctive-uniform/badge knowledge presumption, not automatic guilt. The consent defense in §22.06 requires effective consent or a reasonable belief in consent and its injury/risk conditions; it is unavailable for the specified criminal-street-gang initiation or continued-membership conduct. Other justification and case-specific defenses require separate review.
